storageMap.evidence: Source inspection plus historical folderFlowReview and file-only mapTrash runtimeReview. Current folder Trash and Uninstaller verification is tracked in folderTrashUninstallerReview; historical captures do not represent newly added controls.
storageMap.chart: Binary partition of positive-byte children. Show all through 12; above 12, show the largest 11 and sum remaining positive children into Other items. Partition area follows byte weights; gutters reduce the visible fill area.
storageMap.otherAction: Scroll to the complete size-sorted child list.
storageMap.navigation: Breadcrumb location is independent of scan results. Opening a child folder or ancestor starts a fresh scan at that destination. Back works during scanning. Files and packages reveal in Finder; packages remain non-drillable. Manual Rescan and Command-R scan the current folder without resetting the trail. Current crumb is non-interactive 13pt semibold text; ancestors are 12pt links. The horizontal breadcrumb scroll view keeps the current location visible.
storageMap.scope: Initial scope shows folder choice, Home and Downloads, and Include hidden items enabled by default. Once a location is active, one unfilled breadcrumb toolbar contains current-folder Finder reveal, an icon-only Scan options menu, and Choose folder. Changing hidden-items clears incompatible results and timestamp, then automatically rescans the current folder. Choose folder is disabled during scanning; ancestor navigation and options remain available.
storageMap.attribution: Each folder scan receives a fresh entry/depth allowance and new hard-link attribution. Hard links counted elsewhere in that scan carry an explicit label; folders show shared-entry counts. Independently scanned totals can differ from the earlier parent result and are not merged into that snapshot. A zero current total uses a text explanation instead of a chart.
storageMap.partialStates: Visible Partial scan label, partial row detail, and notice banner. Issue messages and paths remain visible in the notice sheet; contextual help explains that partial sizes include only inspected files. Empty partial states use exclamationmark.circle; complete empty states use folder.
storageMap.percentage: One decimal, <0.1% for positive shares below 0.1%, em dash when the current total is zero.
storageMap.copy: No page subtitle, duplicate root/current-folder heading, chart caption, repeated scan reassurance, or generic item-type detail. Header has a compact Demo label only in demo mode. Rows show extra detail only for shared entries or partial scans. Footer retains the last completed scan time and uses Scan folder or Rescan.
storageMap.help: Header HelpTip explains automatic folder scanning and manual current-folder refresh and the confirmed file or folder context action. Size HelpTip explains independent hard-link attribution. Scan options has a tooltip and accessibility label; folder row/tile help says Open and scan. Progress indicator tooltip carries the current path.
storageMap.refreshState: An ordinary manual refresh of the same current folder with unchanged options keeps its previous snapshot and timestamp visible. Cancellation or failure preserves them when available. Entering another folder or changing scan options clears old results and timestamp before scanning. The current breadcrumb location remains after cancellation or failure.
storageMap.scanSemantics: Scanning reads metadata only and never removes files. A separate confirmed context-menu action can move one eligible ordinary file or folder to macOS Trash.

copyPolicy.source: Explicit user preference, persisted in AGENTS.md and PRODUCT.md.
copyPolicy.principle: Keep the interface clean and simple. Retain concise necessary action, field, navigation, and data labels; avoid slogans, redundant explanations, and repeated reassurance.
copyPolicy.secondaryHelp: Use contextual native help or a questionmark.circle button where useful. Provide hover information and accessible keyboard/click access.
copyPolicy.essentialVisibility: Errors, partial results, and destructive consequences remain visible when needed for decisions.
copyPolicy.restraint: Remove unnecessary copy before adding containers, badges, or help icons.

mapTrash.preparation: Immutable request is prepared from a current scan result and fresh item/path checks. Folders receive a full hidden-inclusive subtree inspection. Footer shows Checking item… and offers Cancel; cancellation propagates to the worker.
mapTrash.execution: Fresh item, scanned-root, and ancestor checks precede FileManager.trashItem. Folder contents must match their preflight manifest. Unsupported, unreadable, over-limit, changed, or replaced items are refused. No elevated privileges, permanent-deletion fallback, or Trash emptying.
mapTrash.busy: Navigation and new scans are guarded during preparation and the move. Ordinary scan Back behavior is preserved.
mapTrash.outcome: Success clears the old result and timestamp, rescans the current folder, and names the moved item in a notice. Failure uses Unable to move item to Trash, preserves results, and reports the reason.

uninstaller.scope: Discover apps in /Applications and ~/Applications. Match only exact bundle-identifier paths in Caches, Preferences, Application Support, Saved Application State, Logs, WebKit, and HTTPStorages under the current user Library. Read Info.plist for app identity; never launch the app for inspection.
uninstaller.selection: Choose one app. Related-file checkboxes are optional, initially empty on each inspection, and disabled for incomplete items. App removal is always included in review.
uninstaller.copy: App uninstaller title, Search apps, app count, app identity/path/size, Related files, needed progress/status, and Review…. Scope and matching details live in two contextual help controls.
uninstaller.states: First visit discovers apps. Selected app inspection shows Checking files…. Running apps show a visible quit-and-check-again requirement. Notices and errors stay visible. Cancel scan is available for discovery and inspection; removal guards refresh and selection. Switching tools preserves state.
uninstaller.confirmation: Uninstall “[app]”? with visible app-only or selected-related-file consequence, each item path and size, total, and Finder restoration. Return and Escape cancel; Move to Trash requires explicit activation and is disabled in demo.
uninstaller.execution: App Info.plist is bound to inventory identity. All selected manifests are checked before the first move and each item is checked again immediately before its move. The app moves first; its failure leaves related files untouched. Internal symbolic links are recorded without following their targets. No permanent-delete fallback, elevation, or Trash emptying.

additionalTools.evidence: Source inspection records implementation scope only. Runtime, test, build, and visual evidence for these six tools is tracked separately under .impeccable/review.
additionalTools.style: Extend the existing system typography, adaptive native surfaces, teal accent, SF Symbols, HelpTip, concise labels, and fixed footers. No new brand or separate visual style.

duplicateFinder.flow: Folder choice, cancellable content scan, grouped file rows, initially empty selection, exact review, explicit Trash.
duplicateFinder.constraint: Keep at least one copy per group; recheck affected contents including a retained copy before moving. Skip links, Finder aliases, resource-fork files, hidden items, packages, cloud locations, other volumes, and repeated hard-link identities. Notices remain visible.

startupManager.flow: Read launch configurations; search labels/programs; filter scope; inspect configured trigger; reveal a file or open native Login Items settings.
startupManager.constraint: Configuration data is not live launchd status or an exhaustive modern login/background-item list. No service edits, unloads, or administrator requests. Invalid or unreadable entries remain visible.

systemMonitor.flow: Five flat metric rows and an optional native menu-bar extra; no decorative charts or invented health score.
systemMonitor.semantics: CPU averaged across cores; memory includes active/wired/compressed pages; home-volume storage; available physical disk drivers; active Ethernet/Wi-Fi/cellular links, excluding loopback/bridges/VPN tunnels.
systemMonitor.lifecycle: Sample every two seconds while selected or menu-bar item enabled. Rates need two compatible readings and reset after long gaps. Unavailable values remain explicit. Stop on quit; no network requests.
systemMonitor.menuPreference: @AppStorage("showSystemMonitorMenuBar"), default false; enabled keeps app alive after last window closes

batchRenamer.flow: Choose files; find/replace, affixes, numbering, or date; Original/New name preview; review; confirm; optional reviewed Undo Last Batch.
batchRenamer.constraint: Extensions preserved by default; files stay in original folders. Changed files, invalid names, collisions, and multiple selected hard links to one file are refused. Apply finishes or attempts rollback before normal quit. Undo is session-local and depends on unchanged files.

clipboardHistory.flow: Starts paused; explicit Start captures only new text/image copies; search, preview, Copy, Pause, remove, or Clear.
clipboardHistory.constraint: Session memory only; no disk persistence; quit clears history. Copy never pastes into another app. Recognized sensitive/transient markers are skipped, but unmarked sensitive content can still be captured. Demo disables real capture and writes.

fileConverter.flow: Native mode picker, relevant settings, ordered input list, output folder, Convert, export sizes, and visible issues/cancellation.
fileConverter.constraint: Originals kept and existing exports never overwritten. PDF compression flattens pages and visibly states loss of searchable text, links, forms, and annotations; size reduction is not guaranteed. Demo outputs stay in its disposable fixture folder.

additionalToolsReview.visualScope: Native disposable demo, dark appearance at 1120 x 790, six tool surfaces, duplicate and rename confirmations. Core tests verify actual fixture renames/Undo and PDF operations. Native image export exercised in demo.
additionalToolsReview.limitations: Light and minimum-size layouts, VoiceOver, native PDF workflow, live system clipboard capture, and actual Trash API were not exercised in this pass. Preview kept open while the user was interacting with it; its disposable fixtures are removed on normal quit.

narrative.overview:
Mac Tools uses native macOS typography, controls, and adaptive surfaces to keep file information easy to read. Forest teal marks the current tool, category selection, storage usage, and primary actions. The interface is compact where files repeat and spacious where the user chooses the next step. Concise necessary labels carry the workflow; secondary explanations live in contextual help. The user explicitly prefers a clean, simple interface without slogans, redundant labeling, or repeated reassurance.

This document records the nine implemented SwiftUI tools on macOS 14 or later. The name is provisional. Native source is authoritative: `Sources/MacTools/UI/Theme.swift`, the shared `AppShellView.swift`, each tool’s view and model in that directory, and `Sources/MacTools/MacToolsApp.swift`. All layout measurements are macOS logical points. Frontmatter captures explicit reusable values; native colors and control styling remain owned by AppKit and SwiftUI. No fixed neutral colors, custom font, or separate visual identity for individual tools has been established. New tool descriptions below record source behavior; they do not imply a completed runtime or visual verification pass.
keyCharacteristics: Concise action and data labels, with contextual help for secondary explanations.
Adaptive native surfaces with a single forest-teal accent.
System type, tabular size readouts, and SF Symbols.
Compact, separated file rows with visible names, paths, and sizes.
Explicit selection and a review sheet before moving files to Trash.
A proportional storage map with a complete child-item list and confirmed file and folder Trash actions.
A searchable app list, optional related-file selection, and explicit uninstall review.
Duplicate groups with explicit selection and a required retained copy.
Before-and-after rename previews, confirmation, and reviewed latest-batch Undo.
Scoped startup configuration review and local system readings with an optional native menu-bar item.
Clipboard history that starts paused and remains session-local.
Original-preserving exports, with PDF flattening consequences visible before conversion.

rules.name: The Adaptive Surface Rule
rules.body: Resolve surfaces, text, separators, and control states through native semantic APIs; use the appearance-specific accent through `Palette.accent`.

rules.name: The File Legibility Rule
rules.body: Keep the filename visually stronger than its path, and right-align file sizes so a list can be compared quickly.

rules.name: The Necessary Labels Rule
rules.body: Keep action and data labels concise; put secondary explanations in accessible contextual help. Keep errors, partial results, and destructive consequences visible at the point where they affect a decision.

rules.name: The Review Before Cleanup Rule
rules.body: A scan or filter never authorizes removal. Show the exact file scope and require explicit confirmation before moving files to Trash, through Cleaner review, the Storage Map item confirmation, Uninstaller review, or Duplicate Finder review. Renaming also requires a before-and-after review and confirmation.

rules.name: The Measured Area Rule
rules.body: Derive map geometry from scanned byte totals, keep the full child list available, and name partial or shared-size attribution instead of presenting those values as complete folder usage.

dos: **Do** keep necessary labels concise and provide secondary explanations through contextual help with hover, keyboard, and click access.
**Do** use native semantic surfaces and the adaptive accent in both appearances.
**Do** keep file names, paths, sizes, and selection state legible together.
**Do** preserve the fixed footer and the distinction between scan scope, results, and review.
**Do** use SF Symbols and native interaction states for controls.
**Do** state partial scans, cancellation, failures, and demo limitations in visible text.
**Do** pair the proportional map with its complete, size-sorted child list and accessible item actions.
donts: **Don't** add slogans, redundant labels, repeated reassurance, or unnecessary help icons.
**Don't** hide essential errors, partial-result status, or destructive consequences in tooltips.
**Don't** hard-code neutral colors sampled from a light or dark screenshot.
**Don't** imply that an empty or partial scan proves the Mac is clean.
**Don't** automatically select results or substitute a cleanup total for an explicit review.
**Don't** claim that moving files to Trash immediately frees disk space.
**Don't** promote the provisional name or undecided future tools into new brand commitments.
**Don't** use tile shades as safety or file-type categories, or equate a partial total with complete folder usage.
**Don't** imply startup configuration equals current service state, an unavailable metric equals zero, or PDF compression always saves space.
**Don't** enable clipboard recording automatically, persist clipboard history, or hide the PDF flattening consequence in help.
